en: transfer into a university (at a later year); incorporate

examples.en: My younger sibling transferred to a different university this year.
I want to transfer into the second year of university.
I haven't picked the school to transfer to yet.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 서울시에 편입한 지 오래됐어요.
examples.en: This area was incorporated into Seoul a long time ago.

examples.ko: 편입하는 학생은 서류를 따로 내야 해요.
examples.en: Students who transfer in have to submit extra documents.

examples.ko: 친구가 영문과로 편입해서 같이 수업을 못 들어요.
examples.en: My friend transferred to the English department, so we can't take classes together.

explain: 대학에서 다른 학교로 옮겨 들어갈 때 가장 흔히 써요. 초중고에서 학교를 바꾸는 '전학'과 달리 편입은 대학교에서 쓰고, 보통 시험을 봐요. 지역이 더 큰 도시에 들어갈 때도 쓰지만 드물어요.
explain_en: Most often used for moving into a university in a later year, usually through an exam. Unlike 전학, which is for changing schools from elementary to high school, 편입 is for university. It can also describe an area being absorbed into a larger city, but that is less common.

examples.ko: 회의에서 그 문제를 거론한 사람은 없었어요.
examples.en: Nobody brought up that problem in the meeting.

examples.ko: 친구 앞에서 옛날 일을 거론하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't bring up old matters in front of your friend.
The boss brought up the salary topic first.
I'll bring this up again later.
It was an awkward topic to raise, so everyone was quiet.

examples.ko: 선생님이 시험 범위를 거론하자 학생들이 집중했어요.
examples.en: When the teacher mentioned the exam scope, the students focused.

explain: '말하다'보다 딱딱해서 회의나 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 문제나 이름처럼 조심스러운 주제를 화제로 꺼낼 때 잘 어울려요. 친구와 편하게 이야기할 때는 '말을 꺼내다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It sounds stiffer than 말하다 and shows up often in meetings and the news. It fits when you raise a delicate topic or a name. In casual talk with friends, 말을 꺼내다 sounds more natural.

en: be arranged (in order); be lined up

examples.en: The books are arranged in Korean alphabetical order.
The numbers are arranged starting from the smallest.
The words were arranged in alphabetical order.

examples.ko: 의자가 원 모양으로 배열되는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the chairs being arranged in a circle.

examples.ko: 가게에 상품이 깔끔하게 배열된 모습이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like how neatly the goods are arranged in the shop.

examples.ko: 문장 속 단어가 다르게 배열되면 뜻이 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the words in a sentence are arranged differently, the meaning can change.

explain: '정리되다'는 어지러운 것이 깨끗하게 치워진 상태, 배열되다는 일정한 순서나 모양으로 놓인 상태예요. 하는 쪽은 '배열하다'를 써요. 책, 단어, 숫자처럼 순서가 있는 것에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: 정리되다 describes a messy thing that has been tidied up, while 배열되다 describes things placed in a set order or shape. The active form is 배열하다. It suits things with an order, such as books, words and numbers.

examples.en: This city prospered greatly through trade.
For a country to prosper, education is important.

examples.ko: 번영하는 나라에는 젊은 사람이 많이 모여요.
examples.en: Many young people gather in prospering countries.

examples.ko: 항구 도시가 번영한 이유를 책에서 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read in a book why the port city thrived.

examples.ko: 마을이 번영하자 새 가게가 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: When the village prospered, many new shops opened.

examples.ko: 모두가 함께 번영하길 바라는 마음으로 일해요.
examples.en: I work hoping that everyone will prosper together.

explain: 나라, 도시, 회사처럼 큰 집단이 잘되고 커질 때 써요. 개인에게는 잘 안 쓰고 '성공하다'나 '잘되다'를 써요. 반대말은 '쇠퇴하다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when a large group such as a country, city or company does well and grows. For an individual, say 성공하다 or 잘되다 instead. The opposite is 쇠퇴하다.

examples.ko: 경찰이 사건 영상을 입수한 뒤 조사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The police began investigating after obtaining the footage of the incident.
I lined up from morning to get hold of a ticket.
Where did you get that news?

examples.ko: 새 정보를 입수하면 바로 알려 드릴게요.
examples.en: If I get new information, I'll let you know right away.

examples.ko: 귀한 책을 겨우 입수했는데 너무 낡았어요.
examples.en: I finally got hold of a rare book, but it's very worn.
It's hard to get hold of, so it's expensive.

explain: '얻다'나 '구하다'보다 딱딱하고, 정보나 자료, 귀한 물건을 손에 넣었다는 느낌이 강해요. 뉴스에서 '영상을 입수했다'처럼 자주 들려요. 선물을 받거나 밥을 먹을 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than 얻다 or 구하다 and stresses getting hold of information, materials or a rare item. You often hear it in the news, as in '영상을 입수했다'. It is not used for receiving a gift or having a meal.

en: succeed to; inherit and carry on (a tradition, a position)

examples.ko: 아들이 아버지의 뒤를 이어 회사 대표 자리를 계승했어요.
examples.en: The son succeeded his father as head of the company.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 오랜 전통을 계승하고 있어요.
examples.en: This village carries on a long tradition.
The one who succeeded to the throne was the second son.
We should carry on good cultural traditions.
The number of young people willing to carry on the craft is falling.

examples.ko: 할머니의 요리법을 계승하는 게 제 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to carry on my grandmother's recipes.

explain: 돈이나 집을 물려받는 '상속하다'와 달리, 계승하다는 전통, 기술, 지위처럼 이어 가야 할 것을 받을 때 써요. 일상에서는 '이어받다'가 더 쉬운 말이에요. 받는 대상이 전통, 기술, 왕위인 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: Unlike 상속하다, which is for inheriting money or a house, 계승하다 is for taking over things that must be carried on, such as a tradition, a skill or a position. In daily talk, 이어받다 is the easier word. The object is often a tradition, a craft or a throne.

examples.ko: 학교는 성적이 좋은 학생에게 수업료를 면제해요.
examples.en: The school waives tuition for students with good grades.

examples.ko: 정부가 이번 달 세금을 면제하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to waive taxes this month.

examples.ko: 건강이 좋지 않으면 체육 수업을 면제할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If your health is poor, you may be excused from PE class.
The teacher excused us from the homework.
There are many places that waive the entrance fee for children.
They say the fee is waived if you submit the application.

explain: '빼 주다'와 같지만 훨씬 공식적인 말이에요. 세금, 수업료, 숙제, 의무처럼 원래 내거나 해야 하는 것을 안 하게 해 줄 때 써요. 받는 사람 입장에서는 '면제받다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is the same idea as 빼 주다 but much more formal. Use it when you let someone off something they would normally pay or do, such as taxes, tuition, homework or duties. From the receiver's side, say 면제받다.

examples.en: Dinosaurs went extinct a very long time ago.
This bird might go extinct soon.
We have to protect animals that are dying out.
As the forest vanished, many plants became extinct.
People are working so that tigers don't go extinct.
Bones of an extinct animal are in the museum.

explain: 동물이나 식물이 완전히 사라질 때 써요. 그렇게 만드는 쪽은 '멸종시키다'예요. '멸종 위기'처럼 명사로도 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 물건이나 문화가 사라질 때는 '사라지다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when an animal or plant disappears completely. The causing side is 멸종시키다. As a noun, it often appears in the news in phrases like 멸종 위기. For objects or customs that vanish, say 사라지다.

examples.ko: 죽은 줄 알았던 화분이 비를 맞고 소생했어요.
examples.en: The pot plant I thought was dead revived in the rain.
When spring comes, all of nature comes back to life.

examples.ko: 쓰러졌던 환자가 응급 치료로 소생해서 의사들이 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: The patient who had collapsed was revived by emergency treatment, and the doctors were glad.

examples.ko: 다친 새가 소생하길 바라며 따뜻하게 해 줬어요.
examples.en: I kept the injured bird warm, hoping it would revive.

examples.ko: 도시 경제가 소생하는 데 몇 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took several years for the city's economy to revive.
New leaves came out on the tree that revived.

explain: 죽은 듯하던 사람, 식물, 자연이 다시 살아날 때 써요. 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. 아팠던 사람이 기운을 되찾는 정도라면 '회복하다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Use it when something that seemed dead, such as a person, a plant or nature, comes back to life. It appears more in writing and the news. If a sick person merely regains strength, 회복하다 sounds more natural.

en: be reversed; turn around (in a game or situation)

examples.en: The game turned around at the last moment.
I was surprised that the two teams' rankings were reversed.
What will you do if the situation gets reversed?

examples.ko: 역전된 점수를 보고 모두 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: Everyone shouted when they saw the reversed score.

examples.ko: 나이 든 사람과 어린 사람의 입장이 역전되는 일도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes the positions of an older and a younger person get reversed.
The game turned around in the second half, and our team won.

explain: 경기에서 지던 팀이 앞서게 될 때 가장 많이 써요. 순위나 입장, 상황이 뒤바뀔 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '뒤집히다'가 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Most often used when a losing team takes the lead in a game. It also covers rankings, positions or situations that flip. In everyday talk, 뒤집히다 is heard more often.

examples.en: Grandfather always smiles with a kind face.
The teacher is kind and gentle, so students like her.
I remember how kindly he used to speak.
Mother comforted me in a gentle, kind voice.
That boss is known for being kind and gentle.
His face looked kind, so I asked him for directions.

explain: 나이가 많고 존경받는 어른의 표정이나 성격을 말할 때 써요. 친구나 어린 사람에게는 잘 안 써요. '상냥하다'는 누구에게나 쓰지만 인자하다는 어른이 아랫사람에게 보이는 따뜻함이라서, '인자하시다'처럼 높임으로 자주 써요.
explain_en: Use it for the expression or character of an older, respected person. It is rarely used for friends or younger people. 상냥하다 works for anyone, while 인자하다 is the warmth an elder shows to those below, so it often appears in the honorific form 인자하시다.

en: work in; be engaged in (a field); be devoted to (a line of work)

examples.en: I worked in the field of education for a long time.
My father works in agriculture.

examples.ko: 이 일에 종사하는 사람이 점점 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of people working in this job is shrinking.
I went to university because I wanted to work in the medical field.
It's a job that requires a license to work in.

examples.ko: 서비스업에 종사한 지 십 년이 되었어요.
examples.en: It's been ten years since I started working in the service industry.

explain: '일하다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 종사하다는 분야나 업종에 써요. '교육에 종사하다'처럼 조사 '에'를 붙이고, 회사 이름 앞에는 쓰지 않아요. 직업을 소개하는 자리나 서류에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: 일하다 works anywhere, but 종사하다 is for a field or industry. It takes the particle 에, as in '교육에 종사하다', and is not used with a company name. You often see it when introducing a career or on forms.

en: be recommended; be encouraged (by an authority)

examples.en: Eight glasses of water a day are recommended.

examples.ko: 어린이는 보호자와 함께 이용하는 것이 권장되는 시설이에요.
examples.en: It's a facility where children are encouraged to come with a guardian.

examples.ko: 밤늦은 시간의 스마트폰 사용은 권장되지 않아요.
examples.en: Using a smartphone late at night is not recommended.

examples.ko: 책에 권장된 방법대로 해 봤는데 잘 안 됐어요.
examples.en: I tried the recommended method from the book, but it didn't work.
Wearing a helmet is recommended for safety.

examples.ko: 여름에는 모자가 권장돼서 다들 쓰고 왔어요.
examples.en: Hats were recommended in summer, so everyone came wearing one.

explain: '추천하다'는 좋은 것을 개인이 알려 줄 때 쓰고, 권장되다는 기관이나 전문가가 '이렇게 하세요'라고 정해 둔 것에 써요. 안내문, 뉴스, 약 설명서에 자주 나와요. 보통 '~는 것이 권장돼요' 형태로 써요.
explain_en: 추천하다 is for a person suggesting something good, while 권장되다 is for what an institution or expert advises. It appears on notices, in the news and on medicine leaflets. It usually takes the pattern '~는 것이 권장돼요'.

examples.en: Health and sleep are closely related.
The two countries are closely tied economically.

examples.ko: 환경과 우리 생활은 밀접하게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: The environment and our daily lives are closely connected.

examples.ko: 음식과 날씨는 서로 밀접해서 계절마다 먹는 게 달라요.
examples.en: Food and weather are closely linked, so what we eat changes by season.

examples.ko: 두 사건이 밀접하다고 하는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news saying the two incidents are closely connected.

examples.ko: 이 과목은 실제 생활과 밀접하니까 재미있어요.
examples.en: This subject is closely tied to real life, so it's fun.

explain: '가깝다'는 거리나 사이 모두에 쓰지만 밀접하다는 관계나 연관이 깊을 때 써요. '밀접한 관계'처럼 거의 추상적인 것에 쓰고, 눈에 보이는 거리에는 쓰지 않아요. 보통 '~와/과 밀접하다' 형태예요.
explain_en: 가깝다 covers both distance and relationships, but 밀접하다 is for a deep relationship or connection. It is used for abstract things, as in '밀접한 관계', not for physical distance you can see. It usually takes the pattern '~와/과 밀접하다'.

examples.en: The company rejected my vacation request.
The documents were wrong, so I had no choice but to send them back.
Please tell me why you rejected it.
The manager sent the plan back twice.

examples.ko: 이 신청은 조건이 안 맞아서 반려하기로 했어요.
examples.en: This application doesn't meet the conditions, so we decided to reject it.
I emailed because I was curious about their reason for rejecting it.

explain: 회사나 관청에서 신청서, 서류, 계획서를 받아 주지 않고 돌려보낼 때 써요. '거절하다'보다 서류와 공식 절차에 어울려요. '반려동물'의 반려와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Use it at a company or office when you send back an application, document or plan instead of accepting it. It fits paperwork and formal procedures better than 거절하다. It is a different word from the 반려 in 반려동물.

examples.en: In the past, the government suppressed citizens' voices.
There are still countries that persecute religion.
Ideas don't disappear just because you crush them by force.

examples.ko: 탄압하려는 사람들에게 맞서 싸운 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a story about people who fought against those trying to suppress them.

examples.ko: 표현의 자유를 탄압하던 시대에 작가들은 몰래 글을 썼어요.
examples.en: In an era that suppressed freedom of expression, writers wrote in secret.

examples.ko: 그들은 소수 민족을 탄압하고 있다는 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: They were criticized for oppressing minority groups.

explain: 권력이나 힘이 센 쪽이 약한 쪽의 말과 활동을 힘으로 막을 때 써요. 역사나 뉴스에서 쓰는 무거운 말이에요. 개인 사이의 괴롭힘에는 '괴롭히다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when the powerful side blocks the words and activities of the weaker side by force. It is a heavy word used in history and the news. For bullying between individuals, say 괴롭히다.

en: be annulled; be broken off (a contract, promise); be destroyed (documents)

examples.en: The contract was suddenly annulled and everyone was shocked.
When a promise is broken, people lose trust in each other.

examples.ko: 파기된 계약서는 다시 쓸 수 없어요.
examples.en: A contract that has been annulled can't be used again.

examples.ko: 합의가 파기될 때는 이유를 분명히 알려야 해요.
examples.en: When an agreement is broken off, you must state the reason clearly.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 협약이 파기되어서 거래가 끊겼어요.
examples.en: The two companies' agreement was annulled, so their dealings stopped.
A rumor spread that the engagement had been called off.

explain: 계약, 약속, 조약처럼 서로 지키기로 한 것이 깨질 때 써요. '취소되다'는 행사나 예약처럼 가볍게 없어질 때 써요. 하는 쪽은 '파기하다'이고, 비밀 서류를 없앨 때도 '파기하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it when something both sides agreed to keep, such as a contract, promise or treaty, gets broken. 취소되다 is for lighter things like events or reservations being cancelled. The active form is 파기하다, which is also used for destroying secret documents.

en: wake up to (a fact); come to realize

examples.en: This failure was a real wake-up call for me.

examples.ko: 사람들이 환경 문제에 대해 각성하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: People have started to wake up to environmental problems.

examples.ko: 각성한 뒤에는 생활 습관이 완전히 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: After I woke up to it, my habits changed completely.
All of us need to wake up more.
He said he only woke up after failing the exam.
I came to my senses after hearing my friend's words.

explain: 잘못이나 현실을 깨닫고 정신을 차릴 때 써요. 글이나 연설에 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '정신을 차리다', '깨닫다'가 더 자연스러워요. 잠에서 깰 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Use it when you realize a mistake or reality and pull yourself together. It appears in writing and speeches, while in daily talk 정신을 차리다 or 깨닫다 sound more natural. It is not used for waking from sleep.
